plain: Citizens United v. FEC correctly recognized that political speech doesn't lose First Amendment protection simply because it's funded by a corporation, union, or advocacy group. Restricting independent political expenditures effectively silences organized voices -- including small businesses and non-profits -- based on their corporate structure rather than the content of their speech. The ruling didn't allow direct contributions to candidates, which remain regulated; it addressed independent spending on ads and issue advocacy, preserving a clear line against quid pro quo corruption while protecting broader participation in public debate. Disclosure requirements, which the decision left largely intact, allow voters to evaluate the source of political messages rather than banning the messages outright. In a democracy, more speech, not less, is generally the better remedy for concerns about influence.

plain: Look for plants that are non-toxic to cats, since curious cats often nibble on leaves. Spider plants are a classic safe option and are nearly indestructible. Areca palms, Boston ferns, and calathea add greenery without risk. Cat grass (a type of wheat or oat grass) is actually marketed for cats to chew on safely and can redirect them from your other plants. Herbs like basil, thyme, and catnip are pet-safe and useful in the kitchen too. Avoid lilies, which are highly toxic to cats even in small amounts, along with pothos, sago palm, and philodendron, which are common houseplants but dangerous if ingested. When in doubt, check the ASPCA's toxic plant list before bringing a new plant home.

plain: Arizona and Hawaii are the two U.S. states that don't observe Daylight Saving Time. Hawaii's proximity to the equator means daylight hours barely change across seasons, so shifting the clock wouldn't offer any benefit. Arizona opted out back in 1968, largely because its already intense summer heat would mean an extra hour of scorching evening sunlight if clocks moved forward, which residents and lawmakers considered undesirable. Notably, the Navajo Nation, which spans part of northeastern Arizona, does observe Daylight Saving Time, since it extends across state lines into Utah and New Mexico, creating a small but well-known geographic quirk within Arizona itself.

plain: Aperture and shutter speed both control how much light reaches your camera's sensor, but they do it differently and have different side effects. Aperture is the size of the lens opening, measured in f-stops; a wider aperture (lower f-number) lets in more light and produces a shallower depth of field, blurring the background. Shutter speed is how long the sensor is exposed to light; a slower shutter lets in more light but risks motion blur, while a faster shutter freezes action but needs more light to compensate. Because they both affect exposure, adjusting one usually requires adjusting the other (or ISO) to keep the same overall brightness -- widening the aperture lets you use a faster shutter speed in the same light, and vice versa.

plain: 'Gross distribution' on Form 1099-SA refers to the total amount of money withdrawn from your Health Savings Account (or Archer MSA) during the tax year, before any adjustments. It includes all distributions, whether they were used for qualified medical expenses or not -- the form itself doesn't distinguish between the two. You report this figure on Form 8889 when filing your taxes, where you then indicate how much of that gross distribution went toward qualified medical expenses (which stays tax-free) versus any portion that wasn't, which becomes taxable income and may incur an additional 20% penalty if you're under 65. Essentially, Box 1 just shows the raw withdrawal total; the tax treatment gets sorted out elsewhere on your return.

plain: The Four Noble Truths are: first, the truth of suffering (dukkha) -- life inherently involves suffering, dissatisfaction, and impermanence. Second, the truth of the cause of suffering (samudaya) -- suffering arises from craving, attachment, and desire. Third, the truth of the end of suffering (nirodha) -- suffering can cease when craving and attachment are let go. Fourth, the truth of the path leading to the end of suffering (magga) -- this is the Eightfold Path, covering right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, and concentration. Together these truths form the foundation of Buddhist practice, diagnosing the problem of suffering and prescribing a practical path out of it.

plain: Mindfulness is the practice of paying deliberate, non-judgmental attention to the present moment -- thoughts, feelings, sensations, surroundings -- rather than getting swept up in autopilot or worry about the past and future. It's rooted in Buddhist meditation traditions but has been adapted secularly for stress reduction and mental health. To practice it, start simple: sit quietly and focus on your breath, noticing when your mind wanders and gently bringing attention back without judging yourself. Body scans, where you mentally move attention through each part of your body noticing sensations, are another common technique. You can also practice informally during everyday activities, like eating or walking, noticing details you'd normally ignore. Even five to ten minutes a day, done consistently, can build the skill over time.

plain: Julius Caesar rose through a mix of military success, political alliances, and eventually force. He built his early reputation through provincial governorships and military campaigns, most notably conquering Gaul over nearly a decade, which brought him wealth, loyal legions, and popular acclaim in Rome. Politically, he formed the First Triumvirate, an informal alliance with Pompey and Crassus, letting the three dominate Roman politics together. When the Senate, wary of his power, ordered him to disband his army, Caesar instead crossed the Rubicon River with his legions in 49 BC, an act of open civil war. He defeated Pompey's forces in the ensuing war, and by 45 BC held unprecedented power, eventually being declared dictator perpetuo (dictator for life) before his assassination in 44 BC.
